feed.title: The T&S Handbook: updates
feed.subtitle: Every change to the handbook, newest first.

entry.title: New principle: 1. What Trust & Safety is for, 5. Detection and prevention
entry.summary: Sharpened principle 4: harm moves across channels, from text to voice to another app, so the response has to reach every channel, and where children and adults share voice, children get the same protection there as in text. Read the post: Voice chat is where safety in games is furthest behind (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-childsafety-gamingsafety-share-7517957140028981249-us_1/)

entry.title: Revised: 6. Child safety and age assurance
entry.summary: Added that voice needs the same protection as text, because grooming in games often moves to voice before another app. Read the post: Voice chat is where safety in games is furthest behind (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-childsafety-gamingsafety-share-7517957140028981249-us_1/)

entry.title: Revised: 5. Detection and prevention
entry.summary: Added voice chat as the gap in most games' detection: why voice reviewed only after a report fails, from letting reports carry the audio to proactive voice tools, and what the UK's Online Safety Act covers. Read the post: Voice chat is where safety in games is furthest behind (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-childsafety-gamingsafety-share-7517957140028981249-us_1/)

entry.title: Revised: 15. Working with Product, Legal, Comms and leadership
entry.summary: Sharpened the claims register: one owner, sales and partner decks included, evidence for every claim, exact wording on age checks, and a recheck whenever the product changes, with Florida's new suit against Discord as the reason why. Read the post: Every public safety claim is something someone can test (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-childsafety-compliance-share-7516878246228066304-lb45/)

entry.title: Revised: 1. What Trust & Safety is for, 11. Measuring what matters
entry.summary: Added that good Trust & Safety is invisible because users and the company aren't getting hurt, and that outcome metrics are how you count what didn't happen. Read the post: A good Trust & Safety program is invisible (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-leadership-onlinesafety-share-7516517440193933313-TnPy/)

entry.title: Revised: 19. Budgets, roadmaps and making the case
entry.summary: Added why a program that works is easy to cut: success means nothing happens, so nobody sees it. Measure what didn't happen, and don't let a quiet year argue for cuts. Read the post: A good Trust & Safety program is invisible (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-leadership-onlinesafety-share-7516517440193933313-TnPy/)

entry.title: Revised: 6. Child safety and age assurance
entry.summary: Added Ofcom's October 2026 finding that strangers are parents' top gaming concern while only 43% set rules about who their child plays with, a one-switch parental control to the default settings, the EU's proposed KIDS Act, and a new measure: how often strangers reach children each week. Read the post: Parents' top gaming concern is the rule they set least (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-childsafety-gamingsafety-share-7515766955706826752-8pJN/)

entry.title: Revised: 6. Child safety and age assurance
entry.summary: Added age checks based on account history and the mistake nobody appeals, and the Kansas settlement that wrote age checks and age-grouped chat into its terms. Read the post: What I'm reading: Ofcom and Instagram Instants, Ofcom's data demands in court, and Roblox in Kansas (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-onlinesafety-share-7513201109180813312-FxKX/)

entry.title: Revised: 18. AI in Trust & Safety
entry.summary: Added PolicyLM-1.7B, a small open model that scores content against your written policy, and where to test it in the Workbench. Read the post: What I'm reading: an open policy model, Xbox's adult checks, Discord in Brazil and KOSA (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-onlinesafety-ageassurance-share-7513555853422288897-CN1L/)

entry.title: New principle: 1. What Trust & Safety is for
entry.summary: Sharpened principle 9: one named owner for every risk and threshold, because when two teams think they share a harm, nobody owns it. Read the post: What I'd tell myself in year one of Trust & Safety (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-onlinesafety-contentmoderation-share-7513978054688395266-P3DE/)

entry.title: Revised: 13. Crisis response, 15. Working with Product, Legal, Comms and leadership
entry.summary: Added launch week: decide the friction for new accounts before launch, get it approved in advance, and review what it cost after week one. Read the post: Launch week is the hardest test a safety program gets (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-safetybydesign-productmanagement-share-7512980609300930560-Azbb/)

entry.title: Revised: 2. Know your risks
entry.summary: Added Ofcom's investigation of a pre-launch risk assessment as a real test of the process, a row for disappearing content, and a record you could hand to a regulator within a day. Read the post: If a regulator asked for your pre-launch risk record tomorrow (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-onlinesafety-safetybydesign-share-7513247972571275264-_yf3/)

entry.title: Revised: 6. Child safety and age assurance
entry.summary: Added financial sextortion: why it moves faster than grooming, the defaults and notices that do most of the work, and how to answer a teen who reports it, from Steven's post. Read the post: Financial sextortion moves in hours, so start with what the teen sees (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-childsafety-onlinesafety-share-7513612793984602112-urPF/)

entry.title: Revised: 16. Regulation and compliance
entry.summary: Added the US TAKE IT DOWN Act to the map of laws, with its 48-hour removal duty and a register row to copy, and a new step from Steven's post: each duty has an owner, but the whole picture needs one person, named by the leadership team. Read the post: Since 2024, the job is proving it works (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/stevenmacchia_trustandsafety-onlinesafety-ageassurance-share-7512890720316203008-kHP4/)

entry.title: Revised: 4. Writing policy and an enforcement ladder, 5. Detection and prevention, 7. Standing up review operations and 5 more
entry.summary: Corrections from an independent fact-check: who can share signals through Lantern, which services Ofcom expects to use hash matching, which services must report on automated moderation under the DSA, and how firmly one moderator-wellbeing study states its finding. Retention analysis and quality sampling now read the same across chapters.
